passage: Some nights the Moon looks like a big round coin. Other nights it is a thin, curved sliver, like a smile in the sky. The Moon does not really change its shape — it is always a round ball. What changes is how much of its sunlit side we can see from Earth. The Sun lights up one half of the Moon. As the Moon travels around the Earth, we see different amounts of that bright half. When we see all of it, we call it a full moon. When we see only a thin slice, it is called a crescent moon.
prompt: What do we call the Moon when we can see all of its bright half?
explanation: The passage says that when we see all of the Moon's sunlit half, we call it a full moon.
